walker.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW production character turnaround sheet for the Rongboy game, of exactly ONE original ordinary needle-felt zombie design shown in three orthographic views. Image 1 is the accepted original game character and material/style reference, especially its green zombie. Image 2 is the current model's proportions and construction reference, NOT a rendering to copy. Image 3 supplies the desired tangible hand-made wool/cloth finish, not a new identity. Improve the design into a cohesive sewn wool puppet that can be modeled in Blender. Preserve the original oval sage-green head, two mismatched flat sewn X-button eyes (large ochre at image-left in the front view, small charcoal at image-right), forehead patch on image-right, short dark repair seam on image-left, inset dark cloth mouth and crooked cream felt teeth. Keep brown open vest, plum long trousers with one green and one mustard knee patch, green mitten hands and green stuffed feet on dark felt soles. Keep original proportions and recognisable face; do not turn it into a baby or a smooth round vinyl toy. Full body in relaxed neutral inspection pose, arms only slightly forward and away from torso so the torso/garment edges can be seen. Dense SHORT needle-felt fibers, subtle coarse fleece relief, felt appliqué thickness and visible large sewn stitches; consistent clean colors without stains or random mottling. Use simple stuffed volumes and restrained folds that a real-time game model can reproduce. Wide 3:2 landscape sheet on plain warm ivory, soft neutral studio light, no dramatic golden glow. THREE evenly spaced full-body views, left to right FRONT, LEFT SIDE PROFILE FACING LEFT, BACK. Exact same puppet, body proportions, clothes and asymmetrical details across all views; equal scale, same top and foot baseline, minimal perspective, complete uncropped feet and head. Rear view has no eyes/face/teeth. Small labels 'FRONT', 'SIDE', 'BACK' only. No pedestal, extra characters, extra costume, weapons, scenery, logo or watermark. This is the visual modeling target, not a screenshot of the current low-detail mesh.
